static_traits.name: Lin Kai
static_traits.family_status: Lives with parents and two younger siblings
static_traits.social_status: Has a supportive group of training partners and a coaching team, but recently Relationship tension with training partners due to Lack of motivation and negative self-evaluation
static_traits.medical_history: Denies past similar psychological problems; no prior psychotherapy; no obvious major physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, good logic, steady pace, high cooperation; but tends toward negative evaluation and 'all-or-nothing' phrasing, often using Self-denial statements

basic_info.main_problem: After losing a sprint competition to a competitor, I feel I am a terrible runner, which has led to ongoing feelings of failure and incompetence.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because I realize negative thoughts about my running ability are affecting my athletic performance and mental health. I want to enjoy running again and no longer keep feeling like a failure.
growth_experiences: Past several seasons performed Good, receiving positive feedback from coaches and teammates; has always highly valued running ability and results, viewing them as an important source of self-evaluation.

Losing a sprint competition last month severely hit confidence; since then, thinking of running or training produces failure and incompetence feelings, gradually affecting daily routines, interpersonal interactions, and athletic performance.

core_beliefs: My worth depends on my competition results
I am not good enough / I am a failure

special_situations.event: Lost a sprint race to a competitor last month
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I have not won in a key competition, it proves I am a terrible runner
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Increasing training intensity and setting unrealistic goals to make up for failure
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am terrible / I am a terrible runner

special_situations.event: The moment of heading out to run or train
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If training now will not change the result, failure is inevitable
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids or delays training, reducing engagement to escape feelings of failure
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: No matter what I do nothing will change; I am going to fail again

special_situations.event: When watching others train and make progress
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others are improving but I have not, it shows I am not as good as others; I should be better
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Self-blame, comparing with others, reduced communication with partners
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I should be better, but I just cannot; I am a failure

special_situations.event: When recalling past successful seasons or others mention previous results
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Past success does not represent the present; if I cannot win now, those do not count
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Negating positive evidence, attributing success to luck to maintain the negative self-schema
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Past results were not real; that was just luck

core_conflict.wish: Longs to prove self-worth through stable good grades and gain others' recognition and respect
core_conflict.fear: Fear of being seen as incompetent after failure, losing self-esteem and others' regard
defense_goal: Forcing oneself to maintain high standards through self-reproach and all-or-nothing standards to avoid failure
Avoiding training when emotions run high to temporarily lower Anxiety and shame

object_relations.self_representation: A failed runner with insufficient ability, fragile self-worth
object_relations.object_representation: A harsh judge / others who keep improving and may surpass oneself (teammates, competitors, potential critics)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor invites one to look for counter-evidence or recall past successes
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Viewing past success experiences as unrelated to the present, like 'another person's' affairs, not easily connected to the present self
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Cool, detached tone; using expressions like 'that seems like another person / not real' to dilute connection with positive emotions.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor affirms one's ability and encourages adopting a more balanced explanation
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Attributing past results to luck to weaken the threat positive evidence poses to current Self-denial
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using words like 'luck / chance' to Interpretation positive facts, continuing to emphasize current failure to maintain the original narrative.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor proposes gradual progress and setting feasible small goals
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Tending to negate the possibility of change through logical deduction, avoiding contact with related emotions and vulnerability
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Maintaining a restrained, reserved tone, emphasizing 'uncertain whether effective / may not change feelings', downplaying emotional-level exploration.

manifestations: Often experiencing 'what is the point' after competitions, believing effort will not change results
Expectation for training and competitions declines, hard to connect to past senses of achievement
Although having training-partner and coach support, not yet expressing failure and incompetence feelings to them
Relationship tension with training partners, reduced communication
outcomes: Emotional isolation and deepening sense of alienation

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Frequently using 'should' / 'must' to judge oneself in sessions (such as 'I should be better')
Treats winning and losing as the only value standard, finding it hard to accept grayness and process

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to perform some action toward other people or things, and does it to themselves instead, aiming the energy at themselves.
manifestations: Not expressing feelings to partners and coaches, turning disappointment and frustration into self-blame
When under stress, reduces training engagement, turning energy that could have gone to external communication and seeking support into harsh self-blame

contact_model.definition: The individual's excessive self-Reflection and self-reproach, overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Repeated Self-denial ('I am a terrible runner'), Difficulty accepting positive feedback
Remains skeptical of positive evidence in session and quickly dismisses it

positive_force: Past multiple seasons performed Good, coaches rating potential and talent
Has supportive training partners and a coaching team
Values running and is willing to proactively seek help (starting counseling)
Able in session to try proposing more balanced alternative statements
negative_force: Ties self-worth excessively to competitive results
Catastrophizing, all-or-nothing, overgeneralization, and negating positive evidence as solidified cognitive patterns
Under pressure, avoids or reduces training investment to escape failure and shame
Not communicating with the support system, leaving support resources not yet mobilized
Frequent self-blame and social comparison causing Decreased motivation and Impaired self-esteem

target_behavior.behavior: Training motivation drops markedly and avoidance of training/matches appears
antecedent: Before training or heading out for a run
Thinking of the last game's loss
target_behavior.core_reason: Generalizing one failure into overall ability inadequacy, judging self by all-or-nothing standards, and catastrophically predicting repeated failure to avoid shame
target_behavior.function: Avoiding Anticipated failure and shame, lowering Anxiety short-term
target_behavior.consequence: Continuously declining athletic performance, Relationship tension with training partners, Impaired self-esteem, Daily activities affected

target_behavior.behavior: Negative self-talk and self-labeling (e.g., 'I am a terrible runner')
target_behavior.core_reason: Overly binding self-worth to results, negating positive evidence to maintain the negative self-schema
target_behavior.function: Maintaining the illusion of control and high standards through self-punishing evaluation, avoiding facing vulnerability and uncertainty
target_behavior.consequence: Intensifying failure and powerlessness, Declining motivation and focus, further affecting training and competition performance
